criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: FLOW and CONDUCTOR provide no-code routing/IVR/service management with delegated real-time change and rollback/audit controls.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Strong fit for business-led change under central governance.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: Define permitted admin changes and release governance in implementation.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: Complex external integration or bespoke logic may still require developer/services support.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: Native WFM, QM and VIEW provide business/supervisor administration surfaces for schedules, scorecards and dashboards.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Fit rises for ops teams wanting suite-native administration.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: Buyer admins should demonstrate representative WFM/QM/report changes during POC.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: Complex analytics/reporting and AI-scoring programs still require specialist skills and calibration.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: Change ownership is two-layered: routine service changes can be devolved, while custom integrations/bespoke development can move to technical teams, partners or Content Guru services.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Fit depends on how often the buyer expects material bespoke change.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: Create a change RACI and rate/lead-time model by change type.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: If the boundary is not explicit, change lead time and cost can surprise operations.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: FLOW includes revision control and rollback; CONDUCTOR provides permissioned changes and audit logs, while AI Charter describes controlled test/change/rollback processes.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Strong routine change safety; full cross-module release governance remains proof-gated.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: Buyer should test environment separation, versioning and rollback for its actual assets.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: Public evidence does not establish a full software-style dev/test/prod promotion model across every storm module/integration/AI asset.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: 24/7 engineering support, real-time reporting and strong practitioner support signals are documented, but end-to-end observability across custom integrations and AI workflows is not uniformly public.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Fit rises when buyer uses vendor/partner support model and clear custom-integration ownership.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: Incident RACI, telemetry and escalation should be demonstrated.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: Cross-vendor/custom failures can still create diagnosis delay.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: Professional services are a material delivery option, but no-code FLOW/CONDUCTOR reduces dependency for routine changes; bespoke custom work can still require developer lead time.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Do not label the platform universally services-heavy; dependency is workload-specific.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: SOW must identify custom assets, owner, future change process, lead times and rates.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: Customization-heavy roadmaps can create capacity/lead-time dependency on vendor/partner development.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: Enterprise TCO is modular and multi-component across setup, licenses/bundles/AI tokens, support and usage; storm LITE has a separate public per-agent/channel model.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Fit depends on configuration and negotiated quote, not public LITE pricing.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: Model exact modules, users/channels, support, AI, usage, storage, integrations and services.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: Seat-price comparison can materially misstate enterprise economics.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: Transformation cost can include professional services, integrations, migration, resilience architecture, UAT, AI/data and bespoke change beyond license activation.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Fit depends on whether mission-critical/integration capability gained justifies transformation cost.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: Separate transformation services and internal program labor from platform recurring charges.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: Mission-critical designs can make implementation labor a major part of TCO.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: Run-state cost includes support charges, admin/operations, WEM/QM/analytics ownership, custom integration maintenance, AI governance and potential future professional-services changes.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Fit improves when buyer uses self-service tools effectively and limits bespoke change.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: Model support, custom-change rates, internal ownership and AI/data operations separately.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: Routine admin can be low burden while bespoke change remains paid/technical.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: License/support charges are more predictable while usage charges, overages, minutes, messages, data dips, storage and AI tokens introduce demand sensitivity.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Mission-critical scale can be a fit-up operationally while still requiring economic stress testing.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: Low/base/high demand models should include usage and AI/storage effects.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: Surge-heavy operations can face usage economics even when capacity is technically strong.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: Public default terms include automatic renewal, 90-day notice and then-current undiscounted list pricing, while early termination can retain remaining committed charges.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Fit depends materially on negotiated order terms for changing environments.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: Procurement should negotiate renewal caps, notice, ramp/true-down and termination/transition terms.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: Commercial rigidity can become significant if volumes, roadmap or architecture change.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: Content Guru publicly documents secure customer partitioning at the organisation level across data, configurations, workflows and interconnects.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Fit rises for regulated multi-client environments once shared-agent architecture is proven.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: BPO design must map each client organisation, shared services, users and data/integration boundaries.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: Customer-level tenancy evidence is strong, but BPO-specific cross-client operational controls still require proof.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: Content Guru explicitly targets BPO/outsourcing, but public sources do not fully document shared-agent licensing/identity mechanics across multiple client organisations.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: No negative score; BPO capability remains conditionally strong.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: Buyer-controlled multi-client/shared-agent POC is required.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: Agent reuse economics and UX may materially affect BPO margin.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: Modularity, no-code administration and partner services can accelerate client-program setup, but public evidence does not establish a standard tenant-factory or program-launch SLA.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Fit depends on repeatability of the selected client architecture.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: BPO should test templated launch of a new client program under a time target.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: Bespoke client integrations can dominate onboarding time.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: Public evidence does not fully establish BPO-specific WFM/reporting separation across shared agents and client organisations.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Unknown is not weak; it is a shortlist proof gate.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: Client-level WFM/reporting permissions and shared-agent behavior require proof.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: Cross-client reporting/workforce leakage is unacceptable for many outsourcers.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: Public enterprise terms describe license/support/usage charging but do not establish a standard per-client BPO usage attribution model.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: No BPO economic conclusion until attribution is demonstrated.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: Buyer must prove per-client attribution across licenses, minutes/messages, AI, storage and shared services.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: Inaccurate allocation can distort BPO client billing and margin.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: Customer partitioning is documented, but cross-client blast radius under shared infrastructure, surge demand and shared custom integrations is not publicly proven.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: No negative capability inference; resilience must be proven at selected BPO topology.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: Buyer-controlled load/failure testing is required.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: A single client's traffic/dependency issue could create unacceptable cross-client impact if shared resources are not isolated.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: Modular packaging and usage charging can support varied BPO programs, but public terms do not establish turnkey per-client ramps/true-downs or pooled-license economics.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Potential fit-up after commercial proof.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: BPO order model should define client ramps, churn, reallocation and shared-resource pricing.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: Commercial structure can be flexible technically while still needing negotiated program economics.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: Five causal break types have been identified around SLA/evidence boundary, bespoke implementation, modular economics/contract commitments, operating-model change ownership and strategic vendor/exit dependency.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Decision use remains conditional to buyer requirements.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: Each break is tied to trigger, mitigation, ownership, cost, proof and exit point.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: Without causal analysis, five-nines/no-code/mission-critical positioning can be overgeneralized.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: Vendor-managed private cloud can reduce buyer infrastructure burden, but default termination/transition economics and incomplete public config/export evidence can increase strategic dependency.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Moves down for buyers with strict low-lock-in or self-managed infrastructure requirements.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: Contract source/config/data portability, transition assistance, rates and testable exit artifacts.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: Technical data integration is not equivalent to low-cost platform exit.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: Fit rises with mission-critical availability, sovereignty, regulated operations, deep vertical integration and governed no-code administration; it falls when buyer needs transparent commodity pricing, very low commitment/exit friction or self-service portability of every custom asset.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Avoid universal specialist labels or rankings.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: Use Fit Sensitivity and separate storm enterprise from storm LITE contexts.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: These conditions materially alter outcomes without changing the underlying product.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: Material uncertainties are testable: contractual SLA, surge capacity, custom-change ownership, integration failure, AI transaction/model controls, BPO isolation and full enterprise TCO.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Proof raises evidence confidence rather than lowering product capability.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: Buyer-controlled architecture, load/failure, admin, AI and commercial proofs are mandatory before final shortlist lock.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: Demo/marketing evidence alone is insufficient for mission-critical claims.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: Public terms make Service Specification, SLA, Change Notices, charge categories, renewal and exit services central contractual controls.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Contract discipline is particularly material for bespoke mission-critical deployments.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: MSA/SOW must lock exact modules, SLA, capacity, custom integration ownership, acceptance, AI/data terms, change rates and exit.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: Weak contracting can convert an otherwise strong technical fit into commercial/change risk.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: Material vendor-owned capability claims are supported mainly by current primary sources; public contractual SLA and several BPO/model/portability mechanics remain explicitly unverified; practitioner evidence is retained only as challenge context.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Evidence quality is high for product existence and governance, medium/low for several enforceability/operating questions.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: Event-driven refresh is required for SLA, accreditations, AI providers, legal terms, regions and product packaging.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: Strong marketing and customer sentiment can otherwise obscure evidence-state differences.

criteria_assessments.Assessment_Finding: Content Guru publishes a private-cloud spare-capacity thesis and very large concurrent-agent/surge examples, including 75,000 digital and 20,000 voice-agent programs; exact buyer-specific capacity limits are not publicly contractual.
criteria_assessments.Buyer_Fit_Notes: Fit rises for extreme-surge and mission-critical buyers when the exact capacity envelope is contractually demonstrated.
criteria_assessments.Implementation_Change_Implication: Architecture/SOW must define the contracted peak/burst envelope, headroom, scale dependencies and load-test acceptance.
criteria_assessments.Production_Operating_Risk: A buyer could overgeneralize named scale examples into an unlimited capacity assumption.

breaks.Affected_Buyer_or_Use_Case: Life-critical, regulated, sovereign or extreme-surge environments
breaks.Break_Summary: The buyer's required mission-critical availability, sovereignty or capacity envelope cannot be established contractually for the exact storm modules/geography despite strong public platform claims.
breaks.Build_or_Config_Implication: Architecture must identify critical-path modules, data centers, carriers/integrations, capacity assumptions and failover tests.
breaks.Buyer_Question: Show the enforceable SLA, exclusions, recovery architecture, in-country data path and tested surge envelope for every critical module in our design.
breaks.Change_Consequence: Any module/region/AI/provider change requires revalidation against the contracted critical path.
breaks.Cost_Consequence: Potential additional resilience, dedicated-capacity, in-country infrastructure, carrier, test and support cost.
breaks.Day2_Consequence: Mission-critical monitoring and recovery governance remain persistent.
breaks.Exit_Point: Eliminate the proposed design if non-negotiable availability, sovereignty, RTO/RPO or capacity requirements cannot be contractually demonstrated and buyer-tested.
breaks.Mitigation_Method: Contract exact module/geography SLA, capacity envelope, data locations, recovery architecture and test obligations; use specialized emergency architecture where applicable; redesign or select alternate platform if needed.
breaks.Refresh_Trigger: SLA publication, region/capacity architecture or emergency-platform change.
breaks.Trigger_Condition: A buyer requires a non-negotiable SLA, in-country processing, surge capacity or emergency-grade architecture and the proposal relies on generic five-nines/private-cloud marketing rather than exact contracted architecture and service levels.

breaks.Affected_Buyer_or_Use_Case: Large enterprise, public-sector, BPO, utilities or mission-critical transformation
breaks.Break_Summary: The platform's no-code administration remains capable, but heavily bespoke integrations, vertical systems, mission-critical resilience, migration, AI and custom development can push delivery into High or Transformational gravity.
breaks.Build_or_Config_Implication: Discovery, integration design, custom development, data/resilience, migration, AI governance, testing and change management become explicit workstreams.
breaks.Buyer_Question: For every requested workflow, classify whether it is standard configuration, FLOW/CONDUCTOR, existing INTEGRATE connector, partner/customer integration, or bespoke Content Guru development.
breaks.Change_Consequence: Significant custom changes can require developer lead time and formal Change Notices.
breaks.Cost_Consequence: Professional services, custom development, integration, migration and internal program cost can materially exceed recurring license activation.
breaks.Day2_Consequence: Bespoke assets retain roadmap, testing and support ownership after go-live.
breaks.Day2_Owner: Technical Admin / Partner / Developer as scoped
breaks.Exit_Point: Choose a simpler architecture or another platform if custom delivery dependency, lead time or transformation effort exceeds buyer tolerance.
breaks.Mitigation_Method: Standardize around native modules and existing integrations; separate no-code from custom build; phase custom work; use proven partner/PS resources; lock Service Specification and acceptance tests before build.
breaks.Refresh_Trigger: Admin tooling, professional-services model or integration catalog changes.
breaks.Trigger_Condition: The buyer combines many proprietary systems, custom workflows, regulated data/resilience, complex migration and agentic AI while assuming FLOW/CONDUCTOR makes the entire program low effort.

breaks.Affected_Buyer_or_Use_Case: Complex enterprise, BPO, high-volume, AI-heavy or change-intensive buyers
breaks.Break_Summary: The technical solution can remain attractive while modular licenses/AI tokens, support, usage/overage, storage/data and custom services create unfavorable three-layer TCO or contractual rigidity.
breaks.Build_or_Config_Implication: Commercial architecture must mirror exact BOM, usage, support, implementation and change model.
breaks.Buyer_Question: Show the complete 36-month low/base/high model including setup, licenses, AI tokens, support, usage, storage/data, integrations, PS, internal labor, renewal and exit.
breaks.Change_Consequence: New modules, AI use and bespoke changes can alter TCO without changing core seat count.
breaks.Cost_Consequence: Potential overage, AI token, support, storage/data, PS, early termination and exit-transition cost.
breaks.Day2_Consequence: Usage, custom work and renewal pricing require ongoing governance.
breaks.Exit_Point: Eliminate or redesign if risk-adjusted three-year TCO or commercial commitment exceeds the buyer's threshold after full transformation/run-state costs.
breaks.Mitigation_Method: Model platform/transformation/run-state TCO; negotiate renewal/price, ramp/true-down, custom-change rates and exit assistance; reduce unnecessary modules/customizations; instrument usage.
breaks.Refresh_Trigger: Pricing/terms, AI token model, support or module packaging changes.
breaks.Trigger_Condition: The buyer uses many modules, high surge/usage, long retention, AI, custom integrations and frequent custom roadmap work while accepting default renewal/termination terms without scenario modeling.

breaks.Affected_Buyer_or_Use_Case: Lean IT teams, decentralized enterprises or frequent-change operations
breaks.Break_Summary: The platform becomes a poor operating fit when the buyer assumes either complete self-service or complete vendor management without defining which changes live in FLOW/CONDUCTOR versus custom integration/development and support processes.
breaks.Build_or_Config_Implication: Permissions, admin roles, integration ownership, support escalation and custom-change governance must be designed during implementation.
breaks.Buyer_Question: Demonstrate which of our top 20 recurring changes can be completed by business admins, technical admins, partners, or only Content Guru developers, and the realistic lead time/cost for each.
breaks.Change_Consequence: Frequent bespoke change creates capacity, roadmap and regression dependencies.
breaks.Cost_Consequence: Admin labor may be low for routine change but custom development/support can add recurring cost.
breaks.Day2_Consequence: Day-2 autonomy is strong for configured services but not universal for bespoke assets.
breaks.Day2_Owner: Business Admin / Technical Admin / Partner or Vendor PS depending change
breaks.Exit_Point: Choose a different operating model/platform if required change velocity cannot be met by the agreed ownership and delivery capacity.
breaks.Mitigation_Method: Design a two-layer operating model: delegate routine service changes through CONDUCTOR/FLOW; assign technical/custom integration, AI and bespoke development to named internal/partner/vendor owners with agreed lead times.
breaks.Refresh_Trigger: Admin delegation, partner or custom-development service model changes.
breaks.Trigger_Condition: A change-intensive buyer has lean technical staffing, many custom integrations/workflows, and no funded partner/vendor development capacity or internal integration ownership.

breaks.Affected_Buyer_or_Use_Case: Enterprises with strict portability, divestiture, multi-cloud or low-lock-in requirements
breaks.Break_Summary: A long-term consolidation thesis can break when proprietary private-cloud services, custom integrations, AI provider abstractions, bespoke configuration and default exit/renewal terms create more switching cost than the buyer assumed.
breaks.Build_or_Config_Implication: Architecture must distinguish open integration from actual config/workflow/AI portability.
breaks.Buyer_Question: Show exactly what data, routing/service configuration, integration source, knowledge, AI prompts/evaluations and recordings we can export and recreate with a replacement provider.
breaks.Change_Consequence: Future provider/model, module or contract changes may require migration/revalidation work.
breaks.Cost_Consequence: Potential rewrite, migration, parallel-run, exit PS and remaining-commitment cost.
breaks.Day2_Consequence: Operational optimization around proprietary services can deepen switching dependency.
breaks.Exit_Point: Choose another architecture if mandated portability/exit economics cannot be achieved contractually and technically.
breaks.Mitigation_Method: Minimize bespoke dependencies; own customer/partner-developed integration source; contract exports and transition assistance/rates; preserve architecture documentation; test exit artifacts; negotiate renewal and termination protections.
breaks.Refresh_Trigger: Exit/export capability, AI provider model, legal terms or hosting architecture changes.
breaks.Trigger_Condition: The buyer assumes broad API/integration capability equals easy future portability and fails to contract exportable configuration/data, custom-code ownership, transition assistance, provider/model inventory and renewal/exit protections.

implementation.AI_Work: Moderate-to-high: provider/model mapping, knowledge, agentic actions, data processing regions, guardrails/governance, testing and AI-token economics must be productionized.
implementation.Architecture_Work: High for mission-critical/sovereign designs; private-cloud/in-nation hosting, emergency architecture and exact SLA/capacity boundaries must be mapped.
implementation.Discovery_Complexity: Moderate-to-high: SOR/PQ/Service Specification must resolve modules, channels, telephony, routing, integrations, data, compliance, resilience, AI and Day-2 change ownership.
implementation.Estimated_Timeline_Band: CONTEXT-DEPENDENT, public terms provision licenses quickly but do not support a universal enterprise implementation-duration claim.
implementation.External_Services_Dependency: Content Guru professional services and partners can be material for complex/bespoke scope; routine services can be customer-administered after enablement.
implementation.Gravity_Rationale: Calibration assessment: Moderate for bounded configurations using standard storm modules, existing integrations and FLOW/CONDUCTOR; High for common mission-critical enterprise programs; Transformational where extensive proprietary integrations, sovereign architecture, emergency-grade resilience, data migration and agentic AI are combined.
implementation.Integration_Work: Low-to-moderate with existing connectors/REST FLOW; High with proprietary/vertical systems and bespoke integration development.
implementation.Key_Assumptions: Exact scope, integration/custom-development count, mission-critical requirements, migration, module mix and buyer operating maturity determine gravity.
implementation.Migration_Work: Moderate; can rise with legacy numbers, recordings/history, routing, back-office systems and staged coexistence.
implementation.PMO_Need: High for multi-workstream regulated/mission-critical transformation; lower for bounded standard deployments.
implementation.Porting_Cutover: Moderate-to-high for number/telephony migration and resilient sovereign architecture; exact carrier/region design must be scoped.
implementation.Routing_IVR_Work: Low-to-moderate for standard/no-code FLOW and CONDUCTOR; High where bespoke routing/integration development is required.
implementation.Testing_UAT: High in complex programs: contractually defined UAT plus routing, integration failure, resilience/capacity, AI action, WFM/QM, reporting and cutover tests.
implementation.Training_Change_Management: Moderate-to-high; business admins can gain autonomy, but technical, compliance, partner/vendor and AI/data roles remain for complex estates.

sow_exposure.Acceptance_Criterion: Buyer-controlled failure/surge tests meet contractual thresholds; all critical modules have enforceable commitments.
sow_exposure.Customer_Responsibility: Provide critical-path/RTO/RPO/capacity requirements and participate in tests.
sow_exposure.Required_SOW_Language: Attach exact SLA and service specification by module/region; define exclusions, recovery, data centres, carrier/integration dependencies, capacity envelope, surge test, credits/remedies and DR/failover obligations.
sow_exposure.Typical_Assumption_or_Exclusion: Public five-nines/private-cloud positioning assumed to equal buyer-specific contractual SLA and unlimited surge capacity.
sow_exposure.Vendor_or_SI_Responsibility: Provide contracted architecture, service levels and scoped resilience/capacity design.

sow_exposure.Acceptance_Criterion: Buyer admins complete agreed routine changes; custom paths and rollback pass tests.
sow_exposure.Customer_Responsibility: Approve rules, admin roles and test scenarios.
sow_exposure.Required_SOW_Language: Inventory routing/IVR/service changes; classify CONDUCTOR, FLOW, REST/API integration, existing connector or bespoke development; define permissions, revision/rollback, source/config ownership and acceptance.
sow_exposure.Typical_Assumption_or_Exclusion: Demo no-code capability assumed to cover all future business logic and integrations.
sow_exposure.Vendor_or_SI_Responsibility: Configure/build scoped services and disclose any custom-development dependency.

sow_exposure.Acceptance_Criterion: End-to-end normal and dependency-failure workflows pass; first responder/defect owner is unambiguous.
sow_exposure.Required_SOW_Language: For every critical integration name builder, API/method, supported objects/actions, auth, versioning, monitoring, failure/retry, code ownership, support/incident RACI and upgrade process.
sow_exposure.Typical_Assumption_or_Exclusion: Large integration library assumed to mean all connectors are first-party, equally deep and vendor-supported.
sow_exposure.Vendor_or_SI_Responsibility: Implement configured connector/custom work and disclose all third-party/customer-owned components.

sow_exposure.Acceptance_Criterion: Buyer data is accurate/timely; full-volume sample export reconciles and meets target window.
sow_exposure.Customer_Responsibility: Provide source-data governance and target export needs.
sow_exposure.Required_SOW_Language: Define systems of record, identity resolution, data freshness, retention, report latency, APIs/exports, full-volume export, schema ownership, eDiscovery and exit deliverables.
sow_exposure.Typical_Assumption_or_Exclusion: Native CKS/VIEW/integration breadth assumed to guarantee real-time external data and simple exit export.
sow_exposure.Vendor_or_SI_Responsibility: Configure scoped data/reporting/export interfaces and document limitations.

sow_exposure.Acceptance_Criterion: Buyer-data forecast/schedule and blind QA/analytics tests meet thresholds.
sow_exposure.Customer_Responsibility: Provide historical workload, staffing constraints, QA rubric and representative interactions.
sow_exposure.Required_SOW_Language: Define data/history, workload/channel rules, scheduling constraints, QA gold set, scorecard governance, transcription/analytics accuracy, reports and admin ownership.
sow_exposure.Typical_Assumption_or_Exclusion: Native WFM/QM/analytics assumed to be immediately accurate because integrated.
sow_exposure.Vendor_or_SI_Responsibility: Configure native WEM/analytics modules and disclose data/model prerequisites.

sow_exposure.Acceptance_Criterion: Meets buyer accuracy/grounding/latency, data-location, action-integrity, safety and cost thresholds.
sow_exposure.Customer_Responsibility: Provide governed knowledge, policies, test cases, backend sandboxes and approval rules.
sow_exposure.Required_SOW_Language: Inventory provider/model by workflow, model-choice controls, processing geography, retention/subprocessors, knowledge, prompts, action permissions, backend transaction semantics, evaluation, logging, human fallback/approval, token pricing and disable/rollback.
sow_exposure.Typical_Assumption_or_Exclusion: AI abstraction assumed to remove provider dependency and make agentic workflows production-safe by default.
sow_exposure.Vendor_or_SI_Responsibility: Configure/integrate/tune scoped AI and disclose third-party provider dependencies.

sow_exposure.Acceptance_Criterion: Country-level voice, data-location and failover tests pass.
sow_exposure.Customer_Responsibility: Provide geography/number inventory, regulatory requirements and LOAs.
sow_exposure.Required_SOW_Language: Country-by-country service availability, carrier/BYOC model, number port, emergency services, caller ID, recording rules, hosting/data location, AI processing region and failover path.
sow_exposure.Typical_Assumption_or_Exclusion: Global footprint/in-nation positioning assumed to cover every required country, carrier, number type and data-hosting need.
sow_exposure.Vendor_or_SI_Responsibility: Design/provision contracted country/hosting architecture and identify exceptions.

sow_exposure.Acceptance_Criterion: Incident tabletop and sample change request meet buyer escalation/lead-time expectations.
sow_exposure.Customer_Responsibility: Maintain named client/platform contacts and timely diagnostics.
sow_exposure.Required_SOW_Language: Name support route, first responder, partner role, severity/response commitments, custom-development request process, lead times, roadmap governance, escalation and transition between support and project work.
sow_exposure.Typical_Assumption_or_Exclusion: 24/7 support and partner ecosystem assumed to mean every issue/custom change has immediate direct vendor ownership.
sow_exposure.Vendor_or_SI_Responsibility: Provide support/engineering under contracted terms and disclose partner/vendor boundaries.

sow_exposure.Acceptance_Criterion: Signed buyer acceptance criteria pass; no unresolved material defect is deemed accepted.
sow_exposure.Customer_Responsibility: Own business acceptance and timely test data/SMEs.
sow_exposure.Required_SOW_Language: Define environments, test scripts/data, defect severity, exit criteria, retest, sign-off authority, no-deemed-acceptance exceptions for unresolved material defects, cutover and rollback.
sow_exposure.Typical_Assumption_or_Exclusion: Default contractual UAT/sign-off window assumed to be enough for a complex program.
sow_exposure.Vendor_or_SI_Responsibility: Support system testing, defect remediation and retest as scoped.

sow_exposure.Acceptance_Criterion: Quote reconciles to low/base/high workload and implementation assumptions; no unpriced mandatory component.
sow_exposure.Customer_Responsibility: Provide demand assumptions and approve scope changes.
sow_exposure.Required_SOW_Language: Attach module/entitlement/BOM, license metric, AI token definition, support level, usage units/overages, storage/data costs, PS/custom rates, change-order process and price validity.
sow_exposure.Typical_Assumption_or_Exclusion: Modular storm described generically without exact licenses, AI tokens, support, usage/overage or custom-services quantities.
